brands.name: Natural Curves
brands.short_description: Santa Cruz-area custom surfboards founded in 1972 by Steve Coletta. Designed and manufactured in Watsonville, California, now shaped with his son Kalu Coletta.

models.name: Peregrine RT 26
models.description: Peregrine RTs continue to evolve. The 2026 version features extra volume hidden in the deck for paddling mobility and ever increasing ease catching waves and dropping in to any type of wave from mellow to critical. The extra volume helps create and maintain all performance features. Moderately fuller rail profiles allow surfers to load their board's rails with increased pressure offering more acceleration, projection, and speed out of turns. Speed is a major factor for creating maneuverability. Slightly deeper single and single to double concaves create more curve in the rail line and rail rocker offering more options in the angles of projection out of turns particularly offering more vertical projection. The powerful vee to double to single concave bottom contour is more common offering maximum projection, acceleration, speed, and maneuverability. Rocker, outlines, and profiles and foils continue to evolve. All these evolving design features are done in moderation and tuned to each surfer's size, technique, and skill. Like every design in the Peregrine Series, the Peregrine RT 26s offer maximum performance in any size waves from knee high to well overhead, any conditions from marginal to powerful, and in mellow to critical waves. The Peregrine RTs are a continuously evolving design.

models.name: Peregrine RT 25
models.description: The Peregrine RT 25s are the most recent designs in the continuing evolution of the Peregrines. The Peregrine RT 25s feature nuanced variations to the nose and entry rocker to keep take offs, entry, and rail to rail transitions clean and buttery. Like all the Peregrine RTs it combines constantly evolving Redtail rockers and foils for acceleration, projection, speed and control combined with Peregrine outlines for lift, quickness, and maneuverability. Rockers, profiles, and foils adopted from the Redtail offer maximum acceleration, projection, speed and control. Outlines adopted from the Peregrine with the wide point pulled back create more surface area and curve from wide point to tail. The extra surface area and curve offer maneuverability with lift and release. The combination of these design features from the Retail and the Peregrine is at the core of all the Peregrine designs and creates a board that excels across the whole spectrum of waves and conditions. The Peregrine RT 25s feature lower tail rocker and deeper concaves. The lower tail rocker increases acceleration, projection, and speed. The deeper concaves create extra curve in the rail rocker maintaining quickness, tight turning radii, and maximum maneuverability. The lower tail rocker and increased rail rocker created by the deeper concaves are the key design features that differentiate the Peregrine RT 25s and the Peregrine RT 24 from the Peregrine RT. The nuanced nose and entry rocker of the Peregrine RT 25s is designed for easy entry and keeps the rails clean and buttery in any waves and conditions. A RPT outline is an excellent outline coupled with the lower tail rocker. The constant curve of a RPT from wide point to tail offers great release without sacrificing acceleration and projection. The single concave bottom is an excellent bottom to maximize power, acceleration, projection, and maneuverability in critical waves. The Peregrine RT 25s offer maximum performance in any size waves from knee high to well overhead, any conditions from marginal to powerful, and in mellow to critical waves.

models.name: Peregrine RT 24
models.description: The Peregrine RT 24 is a progressive version of the Peregrine Series created in 2024. Like the Peregrine RT it combines Redtail rockers and foils for acceleration, projection, speed and control with Peregrine outlines for lift, quickness, and maneuverability. Rockers, profiles, and foils adopted from the Redtail offer maximum acceleration, projection, speed and control. Outlines adopted from the Peregrine with the wide point pulled back create more surface area and curve from wide point to tail. The extra surface area and curve offer maneuverability with lift and release. The combination of these two primary design features from the Retail and the Peregrine creates a board that excels across the whole spectrum of waves and conditions. The Peregrine RT 24 features lower tail rocker and deeper concaves. The lower tail rocker increases acceleration and speed. The deeper concaves create extra curve in the rail rocker maintaining quickness, tight turning radii, and maximum maneuverability. The lower tail rocker and increased rail rocker created by the deeper concaves are the key design features that differentiate the Peregrine RT 24 from the Peregrine RT. Of note, the RPT option is an excellent outline coupled with the lower tail rocker. The constant curve of a RPT from wide point to tail offers great release without sacrificing acceleration and projection. And the single concave option is an excellent bottom to maximize power, acceleration, projection, and maneuverability in critical waves. The Peregrine RT 24 offers maximum performance in any size waves from knee high to well overhead, any conditions from marginal to powerful, and in mellow to critical waves.

models.name: Peregrine RT
models.description: The Peregrine RT combines Redtail rockers and foils for acceleration, projection, speed and control with Peregrine outlines for lift and maneuverability. Rockers, profiles, and foils adopted from the Redtail offer maximum acceleration, projection, speed and control. Outlines adopted from the Peregrine with the wide point pulled back create more surface area and curve from wide point to tail. The extra surface area and curve offer maneuverability with lift and release. The combination of these two primary design features creates a board that excels across the whole spectrum of waves and conditions. The Peregrine RT offers maximum performance in any size waves from knee high to well overhead, any conditions from marginal to powerful, and in mellow to critical waves.

models.name: Peregrine RT XV
models.description: The Peregrine RT XV is a notably higher volume version of the Peregrine RTs. It is a maximum performance shortboard featuring a fuller crowned deck integrated with a moderately full boxy rail. The extra volume compared to the Peregrine RT is created with extra width and the fuller deck and rail. The Peregrine XV is designed for surfers who prefer more volume in the deck and rail. Like the Peregrine RT it combines rockers and foils for acceleration, projection, speed and control with outlines for lift and maneuverability. Rockers, profiles, and foils adopted from the Redtail offer maximum acceleration, projection, speed and control. Outlines adopted from the Peregrine have the wide point pulled back creating more surface area and curve from wide point to tail. The extra surface area and extra curve offer lift and maneuverability. The combination of these two primary design features creates a board that excels across the whole spectrum of waves and conditions. The Peregrine RT XV offers maximum performance with notable volume in the deck and rails. It excels in any size waves from knee high to well overhead, any conditions from marginal to powerful, and in mellow to critical waves.

models.name: Peregrine
models.description: The Peregrine was originally designed as a step down high performance shortboard 1" to 2" shorter than a pure shortboard. The design offers shortboard performance in both marginal and critical smaller and medium size waves. These shapes evolved from surfers looking for a shorter tighter turning radius to maximize performance in these conditions. The shorter rail line makes it an excellent design for vertical maneuvers and steering rail to rail through barrels. This short compact design excels in larger surf as well. The Peregrine has evolved into a prime every session board for max performance surfing.

models.name: Peregrine Egg
models.description: The Peregrine Egg is a progressive member of the Mid Length Egg Class.

models.name: Pescado Egg
models.description: The Pescado Egg is a another progressive member of the Mid Length Egg Class inspired by Rob Yuen the Speed Egg Master. It's a creative and unique design incorporating egg and longboard design features, a deep fish cut swallow tail, and a twin fin array in an incredibly versatile and extremely fast design. The Pescado Egg is designed to perform in knee high to overhead surf in a range of conditions from critical to mellow waves. The design paddles great, has mobility in the line up, and catches waves with ease. It offers expectational twin fin speed and maneuverability, mid length trim, and longboard nose riding performance features. The rocker, profile, and foil combine mid length and longboard features. The bottom contours are convex nose to tail. Entry to wide point features a tri plane with an extremely shallow concave in the center plane. Wide point to tail features a panel vee with a rolled transition at the stringer and an optional spiral vee from the fins to the tail. The crowned yet moderately full rails engage the board in the face of waves with sensitivity and control. The soft down rails in the nose create lift for nose riding and trim speed. The primary and preferred fin array is a twin fin with exceptions for a surfer's preference. Like all mid length designs the Pescado Egg is incredibly easy to ride. It is a versatile and rewarding design. The design excels in beach breaks, reef breaks, and point breaks in marginal to perfect conditions. It offers exceptional performance for novice to expert surfers. Rob had this to say after surfing his Pescado Egg for a few months, "The Pescado Egg has opened some old and new maneuvers. Last session had a full rail cutback back into the pocket to finish the wave. Another was a top turn on an overhead foam climb where I thought I was stuck up there but the board released. The nose was buried on the way down, but f*#!, I made it and didn't kook out. It's a really fun board and has so many different modes of behavior for a surfboard."

models.name: Speed Egg Plus
models.description: The Speed Egg Plus is another progressive member of the Mid Length Egg Class. It's a modified version of the original Speed Egg that maintains volume while adding a notable degree of performance and maneuverability. Thie design features a slightly narrower nose and tail than the Speed Egg creating more curve in the outline. It features moderately more entry and tail rocker. The bottom contours remain the same in entry and wide point as the Speed Egg. The rolled panel vee wide point to tail is moderately deeper.

models.name: Speed Egg
models.description: The Speed Egg is a versatile and sublime design inspired by and created and developed with legendary surf gypsy Rob Yuen from his lifetime of surfing the points, reefs, and beaches on the Pacific Coast from Oregon to Baja. Rob's surfing history, his diverse design experience, and his interaction with surfers up and down the coast are the origins of this design. Long before the current trend of mid length designs on offer in surf culture and in the surf market, Rob connected with us to create the Natural Curves Speed Egg. The Speed Egg is designed for knee high to overhead waves and all conditions. The design features a relaxed speed box or an extremely low continuous rocker and the classic Mike Diffenderfer inspired Natural Curves convex bottom featuring tri plane entry and wide point to rolled panel vee from wide point to tail. The outline features a full nose and a classic round pin tail and has substantial surface area for paddling, catching waves, and stability and control riding waves. The primary fin set up for the Speed Egg is the classic 2 + 1, but it's also available as a thruster, quad, or twin fin. These are the key features of this versatile design. The design's simplicity is fundamental to it's sublime and effortless carve, trim and glide performance. The Speed Egg is such a basic design it will literally surf itself. The design is relevant for surfers of every skill level. Expert surfers can enjoy surfing the Speed Egg in any waves and conditions. Intermediate and novice surfers can turn, trim and glide in the waves and conditions they surf. Beginner surfers can accelerate their learning curve enjoying the Speed Egg's paddling, stability, and control. This classic and versatile design combines the thrills of mid length trim and glide and shortboard carves and turns. As it's name implies, the Speed Egg is a very fast surfboard.

models.name: Rocket Egg
models.description: The Rocket Egg is a progressive cousin of the Speed Egg. When Rob Yuen who inspired the original Speed Egg first surfed this design he said, "This board is so fast you'll have to register the design with NASA!" The Rocket Egg is designed for waist high to well overhead surf and all conditions. It offers exceptional performance features in a mid length egg design. The Rocket Egg has a little more entry and tail rocker than the Speed Egg. The outline is slightly narrower in the nose and tail creating moderately more curve in the outline than the Speed Egg. The bottom contours are tri plane entry and wide point with panel vee rolled at the stringer from the wide point through the tail. Optionally, the design can feature a spiral vee through the fins to the tail. The Rocket Egg is another incredibly easy to ride, versatile, and rewarding design. The design excels in beach, reef, and point breaks in marginal to perfect conditions and performs for surfers from novice to expert. The Rocket Egg is a perfect fit in every surfer's quiver and a joy to ride!

models.name: Stub Egg
models.description: The Stub Egg is designed for knee high to overhead waves in all conditions from marginal to critical. Stub Eggs are designed the same length as a surfer's every day performance shortboard with a full nose, extra width, and extra thickness. The extra surface area and volume offer paddling mobility and easy entry. Stub Eggs offers the performance features of the Speed Egg and Rocket Egg - trim, planning speed, and carve - combined with the performance of contemporary shortboards. The design is ideal for surfers who want more surface area and volume in a board the same length as their go to shortboard.

models.name: Merlin
models.description: The Merlin is a double down, two steps down from a classic high performance shortboard. This design class is also commonly referred to as Grovelers. Merlins excels in small waves. This design blends acceleration, projection, speed, and maneuverability in a very short board. The short length fits in the tightest pockets and allows a surfer to take a full swing at turns in small undersized surf. The Merlin extends shortboard performance into the smallest conditions imaginable yet holds it's own in moderate sized surf. The length of this board depends on the size and fitness of the surfer. Generally, Merlins are designed 2" to 4" shorter than a surfer's traditional high performance shortboard. The width is 1/2" to 1" wider. The thickness is 1/16" to 1/4" thicker.

models.name: Redtail
models.description: The Redtail Pocket Rocket is the original Natural Curves high performance shortboard. Before models and marketing came design and performance. The first Redtails featureded nuanced rockers, profiles, foils, rails, bottom contours, and outlines, essential design components relevant to this day. The Redtail emerged in late 1980s and the design has evolved over decades of surfing and shaping embracing all the variables of surfing and surfboard design. The design continues to evolve with every surf, design, and shaping session. The Redtail offers exceptional performance in all conditions, in marginal and critical waves, and in any size wave in it's range. Every Redtail is designed and shaped one at a time to custom specifications.

models.name: Grey Beard
models.description: The Greybeard is a high performance high volume shortboard featuring expanded dimensions and extra volume designed for bigger, older, or any surfer who benefits from extra volume for paddling mobility and catching waves. The Grey Beard features rockers and foils designed for acceleration, projection, speed, and control. The outlines have substantial surface area and nuanced curves for maneuverability. The Grey Beard is basically an extended version of the Peregrine RT featuring added length, width, and thickness for extra volume.

models.name: Wolf
models.description: The Wolf is a step up high performance shortboard designed a few inches longer and marginally thicker than a pure shortboard. This design extends shortboard performance into powerful and larger heavy water waves. Extra length and hidden foam in the profile provide better paddling, easier entry, and improved acceleration and projection in critical and powerful waves.

models.name: Osprey
models.description: The Osprey is a Semi Gun designed for paddling, acceleration, projection, speed, control, and stability in larger heavy water waves without sacrificing performance. Paddling mobility and effortless fluid entry are premium performance features of the Osprey. Quick response and maneuverability are also essential performance features for surfing critical heavy water waves. A well tuned semi gun is an essential part of any surfer's quiver who charges heavy water, extreme and critical conditions. The Osprey has the same design features found in a shortboard or step up tuned to heavy water conditions.

models.name: Sea Eagle
models.description: Surfing XXL waves places brutally simple clear cut demands on a surfboard. Foremost is paddling mobility, catching waves with fluid entry, complete control dropping in, and getting to and turning off the bottom or face of the wave with maximum acceleration, projection, speed, stability, and control. The Sea Eagle is a fundamental and simple design featuring nuanced XXL Speed Box rocker, drawn out foil with volume shifted forward, and a convex bottom for minumum drag and maximum stability and control. This design is tested by and limited to extremely skilled, experienced and fit surfers for XXL waves.

models.name: Classic Fish
models.description: The Classic Fish was created and pioneered by Steve Lis and adapted to stand up surfing by Jeff Ching in San Diego surfing Ocean Beach and the Sunset Cliffs. The design took inspiration from the "twin pin" deep cut swallow Surfboards La Jolla design. The deep cut swallow of the classic fish creates two "twin" pintails which engage the wave separately when on rail. They are designed for a wide variety of conditions performing well in small and marginal waves and in quality and critical waves. Classic Fish are a relatively short surfboard with a full nose, noticeably parallel outline with the deep cut swallow. The subtle profile and foil carry volume throughout. Bottom contours feature convex tri plane entry and wide point to panel vee or tri plane entry and wide point to spiral vee. Decks are flat, concave, or crowned. Rails are low, moderately chiseled, and well foiled for flat and crowned decks or low, moderately crowned, and well foiled for crowned decks. Keel fins are traditional. The significant surface area and volume in a Classic Fish offer excellent performance opportunities in marginal waves and quality waves. Instant acceleration, speed, and maneuverability are the most notable performance features of Classic Fish. They are very versatile, intriguing and attractive design.

models.name: Quad Fish
models.description: The Quad Fish is a dynamic design. It combines the traditional rocker, outline, bottom contours, and rails of a Classic Fish with the dynamic features of a quad fin array. The quad fin array provides great acceleration, projection, and release and adds dimensions of speed, maneuverability, and performance beyond the traditional keel fins of a Classic Fish.

models.name: Rocket Fish
models.description: The Rocket Fish is designed for waist high to well overhead waves and all conditions. It can be considered the step up or semi gun of the Fish class. Rocker options mimic shortboard rockers, the profile features a shortboard foil, the outline has more curve than classic or quad fish featuring a narrower nose and tail. Bottom contours can be convex tri plane entry to single concave wide point to panel or spiral vee wide point to tail or classic concave shortboard and step up bottom contours featuring vee entry to single concave or single to double concave wide point to tail. Both convex and concave bottom contours provide lift and control, acceleration and speed. Rails are low, moderately chiseled for flat decks or moderately low crowned profile for crowned decks. The rails are well foiled and tuned for quality waves. The Speed Box or Relaxed shortboard rocker, additional curve in the outline, flat or crowned deck and convex or concave bottom contour options, and the quad fin array create a board with great acceleration, projection, and release and adds a dimension of maneuverability and performance to the traditional Classic Fish or the Quad Fish.

models.name: The '69D
models.description: In the late '60s Mike Diffenderfer was shaping arguably some of the very best surfboards in the world. This was an era of extreme development - a revolutiuon for surfing and surfboard design. Diff's shapes were innovative and well executed designs that opened up a new world of progressive performance surfing. These boards featured the earliest shortboard rockers and outlines with curves that fit into the critical sections of waves, bottom contours that created lift and reduced drag, and rails that engaged the faces of waves with control and release. These designs raised the level of surfing beyond anything surfers had yet imagined or experienced. The '69D Series offers a portal back to that surfing experience and pays tribute to Diff's innovative and polished skills and the impact his body of work had on the evolution of the modern high performance surfboard.

models.name: Retro Single Fin
models.description: The Single Fin was the original shortboard design. During the first decade of the shortboard revolution the vast majority of all designs were single fins. Exceptions would be single fins with small side bites, Fish with keel fins, and Twin Fins. Rockers, profiles, outlines, bottom contours, and rails varied by the design and the shaper, but they all had one fin. Applying contemporary design elements to this traditional design yields a bitchn specialty board with sublime single fin performance features.

models.name: Malolo Twin 25
models.description: The Malolo Twin 25 is a twin fin shortboard designed for maximum performance in a full spectrum of waves and conditions. The design adds volume with surface area in the outline and moderte thickness in the profile. The extra volume, relaxed rocker, and moderately full profile provide excellent paddling mobility and glide into waves with ease. Malolo Twins are generally a few inches shorter than a go to daily driver shortboard. The relaxed rocker profile, full outline, with a variety of deck options from slightly crowned, flat, or concave, moderately fuller rail profile, and innovative concave bottom contours yield an extremely fun high performance board that performs in a wide variety of waves and conditions. This twin fin version of the Malolo, like all twin fins, is extremely fast and maneuverable.

models.name: Classic Longboard
models.description: Classic Longboards capture the sublime performance features of the halcyon days of long boards turning, trimming and nose riding. Maximum volume, low rocker profile, full outline, convex bottom, neutral rails, and large deep single fins are the essential design components of the Classic Longboard. High density foam, elegant functional wood stringers, and volan cloth yield a weighty board that carves turns, trims, and nose rides with ease.

models.name: Glider
models.description: The Glider is the ultimate trimming machine. It is a classic design for classic surfing. It's length, volume, foil, outline, and bottom contours provide great paddling mobility, catch waves effortlessly, offer smooth flowing turns and trims through every section a wave may offer. When surf is marginal or small Gliders open a wide range of surfing possibilities and magic moments. Gliders perform best in mellow waves though they have no performance limitations in more critical waves. They can catch waves from any position in a line up and are particularly adept at catching waves out the back often before they break. Gliders trim through and connect sections with ease. Gliders range in length from 10' 0" to 12" 0". Rocker is low and continuous. Foil is moderate and drawn out. Bottom contours are classic Natural Curves tri plane entry to wide point with shallow concave in the center plane and rolled panel vee wide point to tail. Rails mimic shortboard rails - neutral in the entry and wide point and low in the tail. All the design elements maximize lift and trim.

models.name: Contemporary Longboard
models.description: Contemporary Performance Longboards are designed to offer a surfer progressive turns, trim, and nose riding in one versatile surfboard. The rocker, profile, and outline have curves that fit and trim tight in the pocket and on the open face of waves. Outlines are marginally narrower than traditional long boards and feature a narrower nose and tail. Convex bottom contours provide lift, glide, and control featuring subtle tri plane from the nose to entry to wide point and panel vee with soft rolled transition along the stringer from wide point to tail. Optional shallow concave in the center plane of the tri plane from the nose to entry to wide point offers excellent forward trim speed and stable nose riding. Rails mimic contemporary shortboard rails - low neutral nose, entry, and wide point to tucked edge in the tail engaging and releasing the board in the face of waves with predictable control. Lighter foam density and glassing schedule contribute to notably more sensitive performance than Classic LBs.

models.name: Makaha Fun Gun
models.description: The Makaha Fun Gun is named after Oahu's legendary west side reef. The Hawaiians were arguably the first modern surfers to embrace progressive surfing on big boards during the halcyon days of longboards, during the short board revolution, and remain on the leading edge of performance longboard surfing to this day. The Makaha Fun Gun is a high volume full template surfboard. Rocker, profile, and outline integrate semi gun features into the design. Wider than conventional semi guns and marginally narrower than performance LBs the outline is parallel enough through the nose, entry, and wide point to offer speedy forward trim and nose riding and the curve from wide point to tail is curved enough to turn with ease and offers great control and projection. The convex bottom contours provide lift, glide, and control. They feature subtle tri plane from nose to entry to wide point and panel vee with soft rolled transition along the stringer from wide point to tail. Optional spiral vee from wide point to tail offers more acceleration out of turns. Similar to the contemporary performance longboard the rails mimic contemporary shortboard rails - low neutral nose, entry, and wide point to tucked edge in the tail engaging and releasing the board in the face of waves with predictable control. The Makaha Fun Gun is a fun, versatile, multifunction board. A joy to surf in small waves and a very reliable board to ride in the biggest and heaviest waves most surfers are comfortable surfing.
